newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu offers more Arab housing in Jerusalem.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu offers more Arab housing in Jerusalem.

text.p: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, trying to blunt Palestinian anger, said on Thursday he intends to build housing for Arabs in an area in East Jerusalem where Israel plans 6,500 new homes for Jews.

Speaking to businessmen in Tel Aviv, Netanyahu repeated a pledge he made on Wednesday to build a Jewish neighbourhood at Jabal Abu Ghneim, or Har Homa, a hill of pine trees between Jerusalem and Bethlehem captured by Israel in 1967.
"We will build in Jerusalem without any conditions or limitations. We will build throughout the city, also at Har Homa," he said in broadcast remarks.

"I intend to bring a decision in this spirit (to a ministerial committee on Jerusalem) next week," Netanyahu said. "I also intend -- and we are now working on this possibility -- to allow building for Arabs in this area."
Netanyahu gave no details but Israel's Yedioth Ahronoth newspaper said some 1,000 housing units for Arabs would be built.

On Wednesday, Palestinian President Yasser Arafat described as "completely illegal" Israeli plans to build in the eastern half of the city which he wants for the capital of a future Palestinian state.

Israeli left-wing critics of the project said it would spark Palestinian rage that could prove more costly than gunbattles in which 61 Arabs and 15 Israeli soldiers died last year after Netanyahu opened a new entrance to a tunnel near Moslem holy sites in Jerusalem.
But Netanyahu has come under growing pressure from right-wing coalition partners and several members of the main opposition Labour party to give the green light for the construction.
Israel views all of Jerusalem as its capital, a position which opinion polls have constantly shown is supported by the majority of Israelis.

The status of Jerusalem is to be decided along with other thorny issues -- such as Jewish settlements, Palestinian refugees and shape of Palestinian-Israeli borders -- in "final status" peace talks slated to restart next month.
